audit_letter: "Ed — The Graywater audit is finished. The freight receipts do not balance, and the shortfall walks on your legs. Bring your books to the board meeting. Do not make me read this letter aloud. — S.V." (Found in Vane's coat, breast pocket.)
briefing: Graywater Police, memorandum from Captain Ada Kowalski, 7:04 AM. The Meridian Limited is held at Platform 2 and the railway wants this buried before the morning editions. Silas Vane, paymaster of the Meridian Freight Company, was found dead in Car 3, Berth C at 6:10 AM by the sleeping-car porter. The company doctor writes 'heart failure' on the slip and is already reaching for his hat. There is a slit-open payroll satchel under the bunk and forty thousand dollars in rail bonds gone, so you will forgive me for doubting the doctor. Three people had the run of that car all night: Marsh, his partner; Hart, the singer; and Beck, the porter boy. Work the train. Search every car, talk to everybody twice, and do not let the railway hustle you off that platform. — K.

evidence.description: A silver hip flask, monogrammed S.V., tucked between the mattress and the berth wall. A finger of rye remains. Under the rye there is a second smell, sharp and medicinal — the company doctor identifies it, reluctantly, as chloral hydrate. Enough to drop a man Vane's size into a sleep no noise could wake.
evidence.name: Vane's silver flask
evidence.proves: Vane was drugged before death. This was not heart failure in his sleep.

evidence.description: The doctor's own examination slip, amended in pencil: down fibers recovered from the nostrils and mouth; the berth pillow crushed flat on one side and misshapen. A man does not do that to his own pillow dying of a weak heart. Somebody held it down.
evidence.name: Coroner's slip
evidence.proves: Vane was smothered. Somebody stood over that bunk.

evidence.description: A leather payroll satchel, company-stamped, slit along the seam with a keen blade. The quarterly payroll — forty thousand dollars in Graywater rail bonds — is gone. The slit edges are clean. Whoever opened it came prepared and unhurried.
evidence.name: Slit payroll satchel
evidence.proves: Robbery: forty thousand dollars of motive. Nothing about this night was accident.

evidence.description: A Meridian dining-car timetable, folded into Marsh's overcoat pocket, left on his dining chair. The 3:40 AM crew-inspection stop is circled twice in pencil, in Marsh's own cramped hand — his initials in the margin. A man asleep since midnight does not annotate the night's stops.
evidence.name: Circled timetable
evidence.proves: Marsh was awake, dressed, and planning around 3:40 AM. His sleep alibi is a lie.

evidence.description: The steward's medicine-chest log, kept in the icebox drawer. Last line, 11:00 PM: 'Chloral hydrate, 2 dr. — signed out E. Marsh, for his nerves.' The bottle has not come back. The drug in Vane's flask had to come from somewhere, and the book says where.
evidence.name: Steward's medicine log
evidence.proves: Marsh held the exact drug found in Vane's flask, signed out hours before the death.

evidence.description: Half of a Graywater rail bond, torn diagonally, caught on the Car 3 vestibule latch. The serial matches the stolen payroll issue. The tear's twin edge matches a threadbare patch on porter Tommy Beck's uniform cuff — and the boy's cuff is freshly mended with shaking stitches.
evidence.name: Torn bond half
evidence.proves: The satchel was opened before 6:10 AM, and Tommy Beck took a piece of it afterward. Theft after death — not murder, but a lie that needs breaking.

evidence.description: The conductor's key log, kept in the Car 3 cubby. 'Master key No. 6 — signed out, E. Marsh, capital depot.' Partners carry masters; masters open any latched berth door. No bolt was thrown on Berth C that night. A key explains the door better than a ghost does.
evidence.name: Conductor's key log
evidence.proves: Marsh carried a master key that opens Berth C. Means of quiet entry.

evidence.description: A dining-car matchbook, dropped behind the observation-deck rail. Three matches struck. Across the cover, a crescent of lipstick in Vivienne Hart's unmistakable shade — Reverie Red, she will tell you herself, as if it were a state secret. The singer was on the open deck that night, whatever she says about never leaving her chair.
evidence.name: Observation-deck matchbook
evidence.proves: Vivienne Hart left the dining car that night. Her alibi is a lie — and liars on trains saw things.

locations.description: White cloths, cold coffee, a medicine chest in the icebox drawer. Marsh's overcoat hangs over his chair. The steward polishes the same glass he has polished since midnight.
locations.name: Dining car

locations.description: Berth C, Car 3. The bunk is made and the man in it is dead. Flask between mattress and wall, pillow crushed flat, satchel slit under the bunk. The doctor wants the sheet pulled up and the matter closed.
locations.name: Berth C — Vane's compartment

locations.description: Open deck at the train's tail, wind off the Graywater marshes. A rail scattered with ash, a matchbook behind it. Somebody stood here a long while in the cold.
locations.name: Observation deck

locations.description: The rattling joint between cars: conductor's cubby, key log, brake dust, and a latch with a torn thread of uniform wool caught on it.
locations.name: Car 3 vestibule

suspects.alibi: Retired at midnight. Slept straight through. Woke at six. Ask anyone — I mean, ask no one. Sleeping men keep no witnesses.

contradictions.response: (A long look at the circled stop.) I stepped out for air. A man can't sleep on these rattling coffins — I walked the dining car and came back. That is all it means.
My nerves. Prescribed years ago, ask any doctor in the capital. Half the men on this train signed that book for something.
Every partner carries a master. The company insists. It opens doors, detective, it does not close caskets.

suspects.description: Junior partner, Meridian Freight Company. Fifty-one, gray at the temples, cuffs a half-inch too starched for a night train. Counts his words like coins.
suspects.dossier: Marsh joined Meridian Freight twelve years ago and owns a third of it. The company's Graywater books show a $40,000 shortfall in freight receipts over two quarters, routed through a cotton brokerage that failed in September. Marsh's personal accounts at Capital Trust are overdrawn. Vane's audit letter was in Vane's coat. Marsh signed out master key No. 6 at the capital depot and the dining-car chloral at 11 PM.
suspects.name: Edwin Marsh

topics.response: Retired at midnight. Slept straight through. Woke at six. The train stops twice and I heard neither. Next question.

topics.prompt: How was business between you and Vane?
topics.response: Thirty years of business. We built the Meridian out of two boxcars and a loan. Whatever the papers will print about audits, Silas was my partner.

topics.prompt: Who carries keys to the berths?
topics.response: Conductors. Partners. The company insists — a man may take ill behind a latched door. I carry one. So does every officer of the line.

suspects.voice: Clipped boardroom sentences. Five words where ten would do. Dodges money and the night; recites the company like minutes.

suspects.alibi: Never left the dining car all night, sugar. Ask the boys in the trio — I sang till two and dozed in my chair till reveille.

contradictions.response: (She turns the matchbook over once, and the flirtation goes out of her like a blown lamp.) All right. All right — I was on the deck. I got a letter from my sister at the capital stop and I needed the cold to read it twice. And since you're counting my sins, detective: half past three, maybe, a man came past the Car 3 window toward the berths. Dressed. Overcoat in his hand. It was Marsh, and God help me I said nothing, because a singer who sees things on night trains stops getting hired.

suspects.description: Vocalist with the dining-car trio. Thirty-eight, Reverie Red lipstick, a voice like smoke over ice. Calls everyone 'sugar' until she doesn't.
suspects.dossier: Vivienne Hart has sung the Meridian dining run for three seasons. Fifteen years ago, Silas Vane's testimony in a freight-rate suit bankrupted her father's orchard line; her father died that winter. She has said, on stage, that she would 'dance on Vane's grave in good shoes.' She carries her sister's unopened-then-opened letter in her purse. Her lipstick is Reverie Red.
suspects.name: Vivienne Hart

topics.response: Right here in my chair, sugar. I sang till two and dozed where I sat. The boys will swear it — musicians never lie before noon.

I knew OF him. Fifteen years he's been the villain of my family's story, and I spent those years practicing hating him from stages. Hating ain't killing, detective. Ask anybody who's been hated by a singer.

topics.prompt: Anybody step out for air in the night?
topics.response: The drummer smoked on the deck near two, I believe. Men and their lungs. I stayed where it was warm.

suspects.voice: Smoky and singsong; calls everyone 'sugar'. Deflects with flirtation, goes cold and precise when cornered.

suspects.alibi: Polishing brass in Car 2 at four, sir, then coffee rounds, sir. Up and down all night, that's the job, sir.

contradictions.response: (He looks at the torn half for a long time, and then he sits down on the vestibule floor and cries, sir, he just cries.) I never touched him, sir, I swear on my mother. At six-ten the door was latched, not bolted, and he wouldn't answer, and the satchel was already slit, and there was money on the floor, and I — I took one, sir. One. I tore it on the latch running. I brought his coffee at five-fifty and the door was latched then too and he never answered then neither. Please write that I never touched him.

suspects.description: Sleeping-car porter, Car 3. Twenty-four, uniform pressed, cuffs mended with shaking stitches. Apologizes to furniture.
suspects.dossier: Tommy Beck has portered the Meridian run for eleven months, the first steady work of his life. He sends half his pay to his mother in Graywater. His uniform cuff is torn at the vestibule latch's height and mended badly. He found the body at 6:10 AM with the conductor and has not stopped shaking since.
suspects.name: Tommy Beck

topics.response: Coffee at eleven, sir, berths turned down by one, brass in Car 2 near four, coffee rounds at five-fifty, sir. Up and down all night, that's the job, sir.

He wouldn't answer, sir. The conductor unlatched it — latched, not bolted, sir, remember that — and Mr. Vane was cold, and the satchel was slit, and I — I stood in the doorway, sir. I never went in. I never touched nothing.

topics.prompt: You sure you never touched anything in there?
topics.response: Never touched nothing, sir. Not a sheet, not a cup, nothing, sir.

suspects.voice: Run-on nervous sentences, 'sir' every other word. Apologizes constantly. Lies badly and confesses all at once.

testimonies.text: Tommy's account, signed: coffee brought to Berth C at 5:50 AM, door latched (not bolted), no answer; body found 6:10 with conductor; satchel already slit; Tommy stole one bond afterward. Fixes death before 5:50 and entry by key, not force.
testimonies.title: Tommy's timeline

testimonies.text: Vivienne's account, signed: at about 3:30 AM from the observation deck she saw Edwin Marsh, fully dressed and carrying his overcoat, pass the Car 3 vestibule window toward the berths. Puts Marsh awake, dressed, and at the scene inside the death window.
testimonies.title: Vivienne's sighting

title: The Last Train
